notes: Eight own pages read, all HTTP 200 and not thin; no page was blocked, so needs_browser_read is empty. None of the pages states CDK's founding year, headquarters, owner, acquisitions, prices, contract terms or hosting model, so those claims are unverifiable. No claim is wrong or stale, so no cited page was read for causes. For the reviewer only: the raw HTML of the CRM page (key a8ecf5c356cdf039) holds the answer to its FAQ 'Is Elead the same as CDK CRM?' ('Yes. Elead has been part of CDK for years and today is known as CDK CRM'), loaded client side and absent from the snapshot text, so it was not used; read in a browser it would bear on C13 (the CRM is named CDK CRM today, with no dated rename). The about page counts 9,000+ customers, a different unit from the 15,000 rooftops in C25. CDK CONNECT appears on the pages only as an event name. Hedged lines were not coded (for example 'the cited ranges suggest CDK is often around $5k to $15k+ per month per rooftop', 'They often lock you into long, expensive multi-year contracts', 'usually too expensive, require multi-year contracts', 'Historically known for rigid, long-term contracts'). Out of scope and not coded: market share ('largest DMS provider', '15% global market share', 'roughly half of North American dealerships'), G2 scores, the 1970s/1980s roots of the core DMS (a product origin date), lawsuits and settlements, and statements comparing Tekion's price with CDK's. Joint statements about 'CDK or Reynolds' (contracts, monthly cost) were coded as statements about CDK. The cyberattack counts (C26, C27) are coded as customer_counts because they state how many CDK dealerships were affected; a reviewer may prefer to treat them as incident statements outside the 13 types. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser snapshot exists for CDK, and none of the eight snapshots settles C13 (Elead) or any other unverifiable claim, so nothing was re-classed; the CRM page is still the one browser read that would bear on C13. Added C31 (CDK sells its platform as suites for different needs, six instances) from comparison-table cells, including the Tekion-versus-CDK table in q7|ChatGPT|3 where CDK is a column header; a reviewer may judge suite packaging a product description rather than a plans fact. The other gap and table lines are features, market position, OEM depth, lawsuits, hedged cost ranges, or repeat claims the same answers already carry (CDK Drive, Fortellis, multi-year contracts, hybrid architecture). No wrong or stale claims, so the consistency check changed nothing.
